issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a milk-related interface named 'Milkable' with an abstract method messageOnMilk(), but the solution implementation uses an interface named 'Dairy' (declared in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) and the file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java in the solution is empty. Classes in the solution (Goat and Seal) implement Dairy (e.g., Goat.java: implements Dairy, Seal.java: implements Rideable, Dairy). This name mismatch between 'Milkable' (expected by the exercise text and template Main.java) and 'Dairy' (used in the solution) forces students to reconcile two different identifiers for the same conceptual interface and may break exercises/tests that expect the name 'Milkable'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution interface 'Dairy' to 'Milkable' (move/rename Dairy.java -> Milkable.java, ensure it declares String messageOnMilk()), update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement Milkable, and remove the empty Milkable.java. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to refer to 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable' so all three artifacts (problem text, template, solution) use the same identifier. Ensure tests and example usage (e.g., Main.java) reference the chosen name.
